item.title: From social media to flood 3D scenes: leveraging large language models and knowledge graphs for flood spatiotemporal evolution representation
item.dc:title: From social media to flood 3D scenes: leveraging large language models and knowledge graphs for flood spatiotemporal evolution representation
item.dc:creator: Qingqing Ran Weilian Li Juan Liu Huiqin Li Pei Dang Jun Zhu Qing Zhu Youness Dehbi a Faculty of Geosciences and Engineering, Southwest Jiaotong University, Chengdu, Chinab Computational Methods Lab, HafenCity University Hamburg, Hamburg, GermanyQingqing Ran is currently a Ph.D. student at the Faculty of Geosciences and Engineering, Southwest Jiaotong University. She received her B.S. degree from Southwest University of Science and Technology in 2024. She has a strong interest in topics related to virtual geographic environments, geovisualization and intelligent disaster representation. In this study, she conceived part of the study and contributed to this article’s methodology, implementation, validation, visualization and writing.Weilian Li is an associate professor of the Faculty of Geosciences and Engineering at Southwest Jiaotong University. He completed his postdoctoral research in the Geoinformation Group at the University of Bonn in October 2023. Additionally, he spent one year as a senior research associate in the Computational Methods Lab at the HafenCity University Hamburg. He has a strong interest in topics related to smart cities, disaster management and digital twins. He proposed the idea and contributed to this article’s methodology, supervision, experiment, writing and review.Juan Liu is currently a master’s student at the Faculty of Geosciences and Engineering, Southwest Jiaotong University. She received her B.S. degree from Southwest Petroleum University in 2025. Her research interests mainly focus on geographic information science and geovisualization. In this study, she contributed to the methodology, experiments, visualization and writing.Huiqin Li is currently pursuing her master’s degree at the Faculty of Geosciences and Engineering, Southwest Jiaotong University. She obtained her B.S. degree from Wuhan University in 2024. Her research interests include geographic information science and geovisualization. She contributed to the methodology, experimental work, visualization and writing.Pei Dang is currently an assistant professor at the Faculty of Geosciences and Engineering, Southwest Jiaotong University. He received his B.S. degree in GIS from Southwest Jiaotong University in 2016, followed by his M.S. degree in Surveying Engineering in 2022 and his Ph.D. degree in 2025 from the same university. His research interests include virtual geographic environments, spatial cognition and GeoAI. In this study, he contributed to the methodology, writing and supervision.Jun Zhu is a professor and the deputy dean of the Faculty of Geosciences and Engineering at Southwest Jiaotong University. He received his Ph.D. in Cartography and GIS from the Chinese Academy of Sciences. His research interests include computer vision, 3D GIS and virtual geographic environments. He contributed to the supervision, methodology and proofreading.Qing Zhu is a professor at the Faculty of Geosciences and Engineering, Southwest Jiaotong University. He received his Ph.D. in railway engineering from North Jiaotong University. His research interests include photogrammetry, geographic information systems and virtual geographic environments. He played a crucial role in supervision, review and proofreading.Youness Dehbi is a full professor and the Chair of the Computational Methods Lab at HafenCity University Hamburg. He received his Ph.D. degree in the Institute of Geodesy and Geoinformation at the University of Bonn in 2016. His research focuses on urban reasoning, analytics, pattern recognition and machine learning for spatio-temporal data. He contributed to this article’s supervision, methodology, review and proofreading.
